Subject: RFI — content safety / misuse monitoring questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked that we follow up with a short RFI specifically about content safety and misuse monitoring prior to advancing to legal review. High-level asks below — can you confirm capability and expected timelines?

1) Misuse detection: do you provide automated detection for known risky categories (fraud, financial advice for regulated products, account takeover social engineering)? What signals are used and how frequently are models/rules updated?

2) Logging & retention: what logs do you retain for inference (prompts, completions, latencies, raw tokens)? Minimum/typical retention windows and any options for customer-controlled retention?

3) Incident reporting: if Greenfield flags a generated output as potentially harmful, what is your escalation process and typical SLA for investigation and remediation?

4) Policy controls: can we enforce custom policy rules or blocklists per account or per model? Is there support for per-route policies?

Ideally a short written response and any artifact (spreadsheet/table) describing retention defaults so we can attach to the RFP.

Thanks,
Jamie

---

Hi all,

Draft answers below (high level) — I've annotated items for Sergio (technical) and Laura (legal). If we agree, I'll convert this into a single-page PDF + the retention table (attached draft).

1) Misuse detection: Redwood provides an automated misuse-detection pipeline combining: model-output classifiers trained on labeled abuse datasets, heuristic rule engines (regex/keyword patterns), rate/behavioral signals (unusual request volumes or repeated high-risk patterns per account), and customer-supplied blocklists. Classifier models are retrained quarterly and rule sets are updated weekly by the safety ops team; emergency rule pushes are possible within hours for high-risk incidents. [Sergio: please confirm cadence wording]

2) Logging & retention: we log request metadata (timestamps, latency), request and response tokens for customers that opt into full-logging, and safety event markers (classifier hits, policy flags). Default hosted retention is 30 days for prompt/completion token logs and 365 days for aggregated safety metrics. Customers on Dedicated/Private deployments can configure retention down to 0 days or extend indefinitely per contract. See attached retention table. [Laura: any legal phrasing?]

3) Incident reporting: standard procedure is: (a) customer reports via support portal/email, (b) security triage within 4 business hours, (c) preliminary findings within 48 hours, and (d) remediation plan and follow-up within 5 business days. For P1 user-safety incidents we offer a faster escalation path (2-hour triage). We also maintain an audit trail and will share anonymized findings and remediation steps.

4) Policy controls: we support per-account and per-route policy profiles, including blocklists, throttles, and response filters. Policy enforcement can be applied at model load time (model variants with enforced filters) or at the response layer (post-generation filtering). Custom rule uploads via API or Console are supported for enterprise customers.

Notes: do not promise specific ML outcomes; highlight configurability and SLOs.

Rishi

Thanks — confirming the technical details and tightening language:

• Classifier cadence: quarterly retraining for baseline models; high-severity signatures/rules can be added within hours by the safety ops team and deployed to hosted endpoints.

• Signals: model output classifier score, token-level policy hits, per-account anomaly scoring (rate/density), request metadata (IP/region/headers) when available, user-defined indicators via API.

• Retention specifics (hosted): prompt/completion tokens — 30 days default; safety classifier hits and aggregated metrics — 365 days; request metadata (non-token) — 365 days. For Dedicated/Private we can map to customer-controlled storage; we do not share customer tokens with third parties unless required by law.

• Incident SLAs: we operate a 24/7 on-call safety triage; 4-hour initial triage for non-P1, 2-hour for P1 (user safety). Full remediation window depends on root cause; typical timeline 48–120 hours.

I'll prepare a one-pager tech appendix to accompany the PDF.

— Sergio
